searchText: i'm looking at the p2p spec and see this: > A response therefore has the form of one or more response_chunks, each structured as follows: but the "grammar" has this: > response ::= <response_chunk>* suggesting zero or more Ah, good catch. Something related to this, and range sync, is being clarified in a PR the thinking is that you could just not read from the stream (so zero chunks, defo error), could read one error chunk, or read many chunks? It really depends on the method how many response chunks there will be yeah that is what it seems thanks grrr, I remember patching that up a bit some time ago - will have to dig through the commit log _runs and hides. worried I'll come up in the git blame_ what is the purpose of the `Goodbye` req/resp _response_? the request says "hey im leaving, here's why", the spec suggests the client should respond... echoing the reason? it's mostly a debugging help, doesn't have any utility beyond that But what should the response be? Just mirror the remote peers reason? don't have the doc in front of me, but reasonable would be to respond that you got the goodbye and are therefore shutting down (and not some other reason) > worried I'll come up in the git blam when my pr's get plagiated for the git fame, that's the price Add me to the status org so I can push to your PR, lol. Jk, rebased nicely so you keep your commits
